newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians dig in opposite Israeli armour.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians dig in opposite Israeli armour.

text.p: Palestinian police have dug trenches opposite Israeli armour around the West Bank city of Nablus in preparation for a possible resumption of violence if an Arab-Israeli summit in Washington fails.

Witnesses on Tuesday said the lightly armed Palestinian police had dug foxholes and thrown up mounds of earth to face the growing number of tanks and armoured vehicles that Israel has positioned within striking distance of the city of 130,000 Palestinians.

Palestinian security sources monitoring Israeli deployments said the number of tanks and armoured vehicles around Nablus -- the largest Arab town in the West Bank after East Jerusalem -- had grown in two days from 36 to around 50 on Tuesday.
No Palestinian officers were immediately available to comment but officials have said they do not believe an invasion of Palestinian self-ruled cities was imminent.

Israel began deploying armour around West Bank cities and on key access roads to the Gaza Strip during bloody clashes and gunfights between Israeli troops and PLO police last week which killed 57 Palestinians and 15 Israelis.

Under the interim peace accords with Israel that allowed Palestinian self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, Palestinians are allowed only light weapons and a limited number of machineguns mounted on 45 armoured personnel carriers.
Israel's Channel Two television reported on Tuesday that Israel had brought in reinforcements, including snipers, to the West Bank ahead of the summit, scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday.
The Israeli army declined comment on the deployments.

U.S. President Bill Clinton invited Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to Washington to rescue the Middle East peace process from collapsing after the fierce clashes.

Israeli generals have said the tank deployment was part of a previously prepared operation code-named "Field of Thorns" to secure main roads in the territories that Israel has occupied since the 1967 Middle East war.

Israeli security sources say the plan includes a secret third stage in which Israeli troops would enter Palestinian areas handed over by Israel in 1995 under a self-rule if the security situation deteriorates further.
